chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Zurays al-Kunasi, who said:
Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) said: "From where did zina enter upon the people?"
I said, "I do not know, may I be made your ransom."
He (عليه السلام) said: "From the side of our khums, the khums of Ahl al-Bayt, except for our Shi'ah, the pure ones; for it is made halal for them for the sake of their birth."

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the People of the Household; the family of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْأَطْيَبِينَ: the pure ones; those described as pure in lineage and state
key_terms.خُمُسِنَا: our khums; the one-fifth due to Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.شِيعَتَنَا: our Shi'ah; the followers devoted to the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.لِمِيلَادِهِمْ: for their birth; concerning the purity and legitimacy of their birth

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the connection between khums and the spread of zina?
ai.summary: This hadith connects the unlawful withholding of the khums due to Ahl al-Bayt with the spread of zina among people. It also states an exemption for the Shi'ah of the Ahl al-Bayt, declaring it halal for them in relation to the purity of their births.
